title.en: Medicare drug costs have a yearly limit

body.en: In 2026, people with Medicare drug coverage (Part D) pay at most $2,100 a year out of pocket for covered drugs.

sources.name: CMS — Final CY 2026 Part D redesign program instructions (fact sheet)

title.en: Extra Help lowers Medicare drug costs

body.en: Extra Help may lower Medicare drug costs for people with limited income and savings. In 2026 the limits are about $23,940 a year in income ($32,460 for a couple) and $18,090 in savings ($36,100 for a couple).

title.en: Spread drug costs over the year

body.en: The Medicare Prescription Payment Plan lets you pay for drugs in monthly bills instead of all at the pharmacy. It does not lower the total. Since 2026 it renews automatically if you stay in the same plan.

title.en: Insulin costs $35 or less a month with Medicare

body.en: With Medicare drug coverage, covered insulin costs no more than $35 for a month’s supply.

title.en: Medicare negotiated the price of Eliquis

body.en: Since January 1, 2026, Medicare’s negotiated price for Eliquis is $231 for a 30-day supply. This is what Medicare drug plans pay, not what you pay at the counter.
